It seems to me most of the discussion has focussed on the history and relevance of the people invited to be speaking about this topic. Instead the focus should be on the UN/ITU and what their strategy is.

Back in 2012, the UN/ITU held the WCIT, where they attempted to extend the International Telecommunications Regulations (ITRs) to the internet. Some links for reading:

  • Wired: Internet safe from globalised censorship as UN treaty fails

  • Internet Society: WCIT: What happened and what's next (pdf)

  • ARIN: WCIT (with links to more resources)

At the ITU 2014 plenipotentiary conference, there was agreement again not to expand the ITU's role in internet governance nor cybersecurity issues, which was one of the objectives of the US delegation.

However, with many member countries wanting to exert control over the internet through the ITU (and in so doing, reduce the influence of the US) and the next plenipotentiary conference due in 2018, it would not be surprising to find out that parts of the ITU are preparing to try again. The UN/ITU is a large organisation, and plan things slowly and prepare reports, findings, etc. well in advance of key meetings where decisions are made. It is interesting to note that the ITU's Chief of Strategic Planning is one of the co-vice chairs of the Broadband Commission.

Looking forward to your thoughts, information and discussion on this.
